X.note: Clean CG, but the square is a huge empty beige plane and the top half is blank sky. The soldiers are tiny peg figures. The buildings are plain white boxes with unconvincing windows and no Georgian or Genoese character. The cannons are simple wheel blobs and the cannonball piles are scattered at random. The 'not a photograph' caption admits it is procedural. The red, blue and white palette reads as a game prototype. The Union Jack on the pole is plausible for 1782, but it is the only convincing detail.

Y.note: A dense, game-engine-style render of the old town with terracotta roofs, shadows, streets, a hilltop tower and bastion walls. It has depth and scale, and it reads as a real place. The hillside is a smooth low-poly texture with blobby tree clusters. The town looks more like a modern or 19th-century Mediterranean town than 1752 (uniform building heights, some modern-looking blocks, and a large flat grey area near the shore). The faded caption overlapping the lower-left water is garbled and unreadable. The 'No AI imagery · Landsat 5' banner is odd for 1752.

why: Y shows a dense, believable town with real scale and depth, while X is a nearly empty beige plane with toy-like figures and half the frame blank sky.
top_fix_for_weaker: Fill the frame: lower the camera and crop out the empty sky, add 30 or more period figures (soldiers, civilians, carts) and varied architecture on both sides, and give the ground paving, texture and clutter so it stops reading as an empty sandbox.
